https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text: in Rome All of Italy’s daily newspapers have led with AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt, with La Repubblica’s headline describing it as “the darkness above Berlin”. The political reaction exposes the divisions in Giorgia Meloni’s ruling coalition. Matteo Salvini, leader of the far-right League, said the victory was “remarkable for the AdD” and reportedly sent a message of congratulations to its leader, Alice Wiedel. Antonio Tajani, who leads the centre-right Forza Italia, said the victory was “bad news” while Meloni, whose Brothers of Italy party has neofascist roots, has not said anything publicly. Some reports suggest her views align more with Tajani, in that the election result is not something to celebrate but should be a warning that the EU must be more effective in its response to the concerns of citizens.
